Class WorldBlocks

Namespace
OnixRuntime.Api.World
Assembly
OnixRuntime.dll

Provides access to world blocks, including block retrieval, setting, biome, lighting, collisions, and raycasting. You only need to dispose of this when you create your own. Note that you should probably create it on the thread you plan on using it on.

Methods

CreateForClient(bool, bool, bool)

Creates a new instance of world WorldBlocks for the client. You should call this on the thread you plan on using it on. Anything regarding this method or using its result might be unstable if you don't use it exactly how the game approves. You should keep the default parameters for most cases, don't forget to Dispose() it when you are done using it. MAKE SURE TO PUT try-catches around your code if you do this in a new threads, uncaught exceptions will crash the whole game.

public static WorldBlocks CreateForClient(bool isPublic = false, bool allowUnpopulatedChunks = false, bool allowClientTickingChanges = false)

Parameters

isPublic bool

If this source should announce itself for other event listeners.

allowUnpopulatedChunks bool

If chunks that aren't populated allowed.

allowClientTickingChanges bool

If changes made by the client, maybe as a prediction are accepted. Or maybe you cant make changes on client ticks, not sure.

Returns

WorldBlocks

The new world blocks, or null if it failed to make one.

GetExtraBlock(BlockPos)

Gets the block at the specified world position in the second layer (layer 1). This will most often give you water or snow layers, it's used for waterlogging or having foliage inside snow layers.
